reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and RSchedule/recurConfigToRSchedule and adds a shared isNonWorkingDay, but the daily-skip rule is not put into one shared function, so getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template each re-decide it.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && daily ? skip non-working : move' per-occurrence branch is written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange) and schedule-template recomputes the same daily/move flag, with a separate 14-iteration bound in two places.

placement.why: Holiday/non-working logic sits in shared/schedules as it should, but the occurrence-adjustment rule for listings lives inline in server/schedules/app.ts handlers and in budget/schedule-template rather than in the shared schedule module.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the schedule date code, types, tests and release notes; the rule-utils frequency/holidays pass-through is needed.

maintainability.why: A future rule change (as step 3/4 already showed) must be applied in several hand-written loops and a caller-computed noSkipWeekend expression in schedule-template, which is fragile.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and budget/schedule-template.ts movesWeekend, apply the daily-skip/move rule themselves instead of going through getNextDate/one shared adjustment function

disguised_duplication.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange carry the same per-occurrence skip-or-move logic reshaped (counter loop vs set+range filter), and getNextDate's findWeekday re-expresses it again

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter and an unknown-mode special branch; getNextDate gains a daily-frequency special branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template createScheduleList re-implement the daily rule around the helpers
